==Singular or plural==

Okay, we've got 10 links going to [[Trollocs]] and 9 going to [[Trolloc]] at this point; which one do we want to be the real article? What does Wikipedia use, singular or plural? I'd prefer singular, I think.... [[User:Nae'blis|nae'blis]] ''<sub>[[User_talk:Nae'blis|(talk)]]</sub>'' 13:06, 15 Nov 2005 (UTC)

: They used to have a singular article, but it now redirects to the "Concepts" article which has Trollocs as a sub-section.  We should use singular for our article names.  Mistaken links to <nowiki>[[Trollocs]] should be changed to [[Trolloc]]s</nowiki> as we come across them... --[[User:Gherald|Gherald]] 17:50, 15 Nov 2005 (UTC)

:: Actually, I was asking what Wikipedia's Manual of Style mandated, and they use singular too. I'll edit the links we have now, to avoid setting bad precedent. I'll add this to the Style Guide, too... [[User:Nae'blis|nae'blis]] ''<sub>[[User_talk:Nae'blis|(talk)]]</sub>'' 21:08, 16 Nov 2005 (UTC)

== Intelligence  ==

If they can forge iron and use it to make weapons and armor, if the can speak and read their own language and some can learn the common toungue than they're not as stupid as the article makes out. Cruel, sadistic, and cowardly yes, but not stupid.

I would say the're a difference between "stupid" as "unintelligent" and "stupid" as in "brute" or "dumb"
